Subject: Post-call recap — procurement & hosting preference (PO vs marketplace)

Thanks again for taking time today, Sanjay — quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Hosting preference: leaning toward Dedicated (predictable latency for inference)
- Commitment appetite: team interest in a ~12-month reserved commitment if commercial terms support it

Open items we promised to follow up on
1) Confirm options for PO vs credit-card vs Marketplace billing and any differences in lead times.
2) Provide the draft SOW and a pricing matrix for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, with commit vs on-demand examples.
3) Share typical procurement paperwork (SaaS T&Cs + SOW template) and next-step checklist for procurement team.

Attachments: pricing matrix (CSV) + draft SOW stub.

- Kimberly: share the pricing matrix, SOW draft, and a short purchasing playbook for PO vs Marketplace.
- Proposed date: a 30-min alignment call with procurement on Thu 20 May or Fri 21 May.

Thanks — I’ll loop in our pricing & finance partner so we can surface commit-level discounts for a 12mo reserved plan.

Best,

Thanks Kimberly — useful recap. A few clarifications from procurement and legal: 

- Billing route: procurement prefers PO where possible. Marketplace is a nice-to-have because it shortens approval cycles, but legal has to vet any marketplace contract templates (so it may not be faster automatically).
- Contracting owner: Procurement will own the PO & invoicing discussion; Legal will need the SOW + platform T&Cs for a quick review.
- Hosting preference: our ML infra team prefers Dedicated for consistent latency; Security is evaluating Private only if we can’t meet isolation requirements in Dedicated.
- Commitment: Finance is open to a 12-month committed reservation if there’s clear unit-cost savings and predictable billing.

Can you send a line-item frame: 12mo commit price vs on-demand, and whether marketplace purchase would change the URL/contract or invoice flow? Also can you include names/roles for the Redwood contacts procurement/legal should speak with?

Attaching our internal sourcing checklist — it lists the docs procurement typically needs.

Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of ML Platform
Greenline Energy

Appreciate the details, Sanjay — here’s the concise commercial framing to help procurement/legal evaluate options quickly. I’ve attached a short pricing matrix and a draft SOW.

Quick commercial frames (high level)
- Hosted (Redwood API, on-demand): No commit, pay-as-you-go. Pros: fastest onboarding, no long-term contract. Cons: higher per-token cost vs reserved pools.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Reserved GPU pool and predictable throughput. Pros: meaningful per-token discount at 6/12/24mo commits, isolation from noisy neighbors. Cons: requires commitment (monthly invoicing possible).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Enterprise licensing + deployment. Pros: max control for security/regulatory needs. Cons: higher setup fee and typically enterprise licensing cadence (platform fee + support).

Example price bands (illustrative)
- On-demand hosted: baseline rate X per 1k tokens
- Dedicated, 12mo commit: approx 30% discount vs on-demand (depends on model family & runtime profile)
- Private: custom pricing (setup + platform fee), often modeled as a blended rate after deployment costs

Marketplace vs PO notes
- Marketplace: purchase via AWS Marketplace often simplifies procurement approval but can limit certain billing flexibilities (e.g., custom invoices/PO routing).
- PO: standard for many customers; we can invoice against a PO monthly.

Attachments included: redwood-pricing-matrix-20270517.csv (pricing bands), draft-sow-greenline-20270517.docx (SOW stub).

Proposed next steps
1) Kimberly/Rishi to run a short internal pricing call to finalize a 12mo commit quote for Greenline.
2) Procurement & Legal: review attached SOW + our standard T&Cs (link in Drive) and confirm whether purchase will be via Marketplace or PO.
3) Schedule a 30-min procurement alignment meeting — availability Thu 20 May 10–12 PT or Fri 21 May 14–16 PT.

Looping in Rishi (finance/pricing) and Laura (sales ops) to help with a firm quote and the procurement checklist items you requested.
